title: Feedback on sustainability reporting standards: additional explanatory information regarding the value chain cap
key_claim: The Omnibus I value-chain cap prohibits CSRD companies from REQUIRING value-chain partners of 1,000 employees or fewer to provide more than the voluntary standard; but it applies only to CSRD reporting purposes, does not affect information requests for other purposes, and CSRD companies may still REQUEST above-cap information (which the partner has a statutory right to decline).
notes: Primary EC source. Anchors both the signal (the cap binds only public-regulatory requests) and the counter-argument.

title: Commission seeks feedback on revised sustainability reporting standards
key_claim: The Commission launched a one-month public feedback on draft revised ESRS (mandatory datapoints cut by over 60%, total by over 70%) and a voluntary reporting standard for smaller companies that operationalises the value-chain cap; delegated acts to be adopted after the consultation closes on 3 June 2026.
notes: Primary EC source on the simplified ESRS and the voluntary-standard-as-cap design.

title: Global Sustainable Finance Outlook 2026 (executive summary)
key_claim: Businesses will increasingly disclose adaptation strategies and investment to stakeholders including regulators and lenders; fragmented regulation is increasing compliance costs; sustainable bond issuance is forecast broadly flat at ~$900bn in 2026.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6m band): canonical institutional framing of the 2026 sustainable-finance landscape and the lender/regulator data-demand thread.

title: S&P Global Ratings Forecasts Global Sustainable Bond Market Will Consolidate In 2026 with Issuance Levels at $800-900 billion
key_claim: The sustainable bond market is consolidating, with the focus shifting from growth to credibility, transparency and measurable outcomes; in the US, labelled issuance has slowed as some issuers prefer conventional bonds to avoid additional reporting requirements.
notes: Tier 2 rating-agency research. Corroborates the quality-over-quantity shift and the disclosure-avoidance dynamic.

title: What happens to climate transition plans in the wake of the EU omnibus?
key_claim: The Omnibus removed legal transition-plan obligations, but banks still need them under CRD6/other legislation; experts warn of 'increased fragmentation and reduced accountability', more data gaps and estimation, and a growing role for specialised private data providers.
notes: Rich expert-sourced account of the data-fragmentation and private-channel-migration dynamic central to the signal.

title: Omnibus Simplification of EU's Sustainability Rules (CSRD and CSDDD) Enacted
key_claim: Amendment Directive (EU) 2026/470 was published on 26 February 2026 and entered into force on 18 March 2026, significantly narrowing CSRD and CSDDD scope; Wave 1 companies below the revised thresholds fall out of scope for FY2025-2026, with national transposition due by March 2027 (CSRD) and July 2028 (CSDDD).
notes: Law-firm client alert; precise legislative-status and timeline anchor.

title: EU Omnibus Package 2026: CSRD Scope Reduced by 80% — What Changed and Who Is Still In Scope
key_claim: The Omnibus removes roughly 80% of companies previously in CSRD scope; the shift is also market-driven, as ESG ratings agencies, institutional investors and large corporate customers will continue to request sustainability data even though the legal obligation is gone.
notes: Commercial regtech platform (AI-generated analysis). Used only as directional corroboration for the scope-cut framing, which is independently confirmed by the EC and Gibson Dunn sources.
